_about: Scientific data library, domain equipment: the universal columns of the game's body/data/equipment.json tables, written by scripts/split_data.py. Same columns/rows schema as the game's tables. `id` is stable (see README); `source` holds source keys from sources.json ('; ' separated) or 'open'. Mark is the review state of these columns. A null in a column the engine's data/*.json holds by the same id means the engine file is the home of that value.

roles.title: Capability roles: what a piece of equipment contributes to an apparatus
roles.source: ChatGPT's component idea (outside AI), kept: a burner heats, a vessel holds, a condenser cools, a pump changes pressure, an instrument measures; the simulation decides what the assembly can do. Roles are the keeper's typing; each equipment record lists its roles with the numbers the role needs.

assembly.title: Assembling an apparatus: how the engine decides what a set of equipment can do
assembly.source: ChatGPT's six questions (outside AI), kept as the attempt pipeline; the keeper's rule that the apparatus's capability is the minimum over the roles the process needs. Skill moves the minigame's control, never the chemistry (Rex's recipe rule and knowledge rule, GOODS 3c and 3f).
rows: Are the materials present (reactants, solvents, fuel)?
rex (materials + equipment + band + knowledge is Rex's recipe rule), proposed (as a pipeline)

Does the assembled apparatus meet the process's conditions? For each role the process needs (heat to T, hold it +/- x for t; a vessel of volume V that survives the reagents at T and P; a condenser for a vapour at b.p.; vacuum to p), is there a piece whose numbers cover it?
the catalogue's numbers; the process's conditions (CHEMISTRY reaction record)
the process does not run, or runs partway (a lower yield, a different product: what the simulation supports), or the vessel breaks (an accident: ATMOSPHERE's laboratory scenario)
Is there fuel or power for the duration?
charcoal, spirit, the sun, a water wheel, a pile (TECHNOLOGY)
the process stops when it runs out

Can the pieces be connected, and do they agree? Joints and seals (glass to glass needs lute or ground joints: period lute is clay); a vessel's max temperature and pressure cover the heat and pressure roles' numbers; the vessel's material survives the reagents (no mercury in a lead pot, no acid in iron); a condenser's capacity covers the still's rate
a joints rule; each piece's ranges against the others' (two working pieces are not a working apparatus: ChatGPT's point, 2026-10-29, agreed)
leaks (exposure, loss); a vessel that cracks or melts (an accident); a run that never reaches the condition
Can the character control it (temperature, timing, measurement, handling)?
the skill's minigame (Rex's minigames); skill band sets difficulty, never the chemistry
a bad run: wrong temperature, a boil-over, contamination
rex (skill affects execution), proposed (as a step)
Do the actual conditions reached permit the transformation?
CHEMISTRY kinetics and equilibrium at the conditions reached
nothing happens, or something else does (the engine's answer; an unsupported reaction is 'unknown', not impossible)
Can the character tell what he made?
the measure roles present (DISCOVERY: observed vs identified)
a product he cannot name: an 'unknown liquid' in the journal

wear.title: Wear and calibration: condition as three independent properties (proposed; ties the science system to the ship's maintenance loop)
wear.source: ChatGPT's suggestion (outside AI), recorded: a poorly kept balance drifts, a damaged furnace will not hold heat. Statement: gears/equipment-condition.md. A ship's maintenance (keeps / if skipped) has the same shape, and this table gives apparatus the same, so the economy's facilities and the laboratory age like a ship. Refined 2026-10-29 (ChatGPT, outside AI, agreed): condition is not one number; a damaged furnace may still reach its maximum and fail to hold it, a worn seal lowers pressure and not heat, a drifted thermometer misreports while the reaction proceeds normally.
rows: capability (what it can physically reach: the catalogue's max numbers), control (how reliably it holds a condition: the +/- and the drift over a run), accuracy (how truly its measure roles report: precision and offset). Each wears on its own
a cracked crucible, a burnt-out furnace lining, a worn pump leather: the max falls (temperature, pressure, vacuum floor, capacity)
a leaking seal, a sagging bellows, a cracked athanor: the piece reaches its max but cannot hold it; the +/- widens, a run drifts

measuring pieces drift: offset and precision worsen with days since calibration and with rough use; calibrating needs a standard (weights, a fixed-point bath for a thermometer, a known acid for litmus)
each property falls per run by the process's severity (heat over 80% of max, corrosive reagents, pressure) and the material (clay fast, glass medium, brass slow)

a trade repairs or replaces (the smith for iron, the glassblower for glass, the instrument maker for brass: TECHNOLOGY manufacture prerequisites); calibration is a measurement against a standard the character must hold
GOODS trades; the standards as goods (open)

producing a thing (the apparatus's capability and control), measuring it (accuracy), identifying it (DISCOVERY): a character can synthesise a compound, measure it wrong on a drifted instrument, and enter it wrong in the journal until a later experiment corrects it. Success never hands the player perfect information
proposed (ChatGPT's point, agreed; it fits Rex's hidden-information design)

the three properties map onto the reusable controls (phase 7 of the plan): control is what the temperature and pressure minigames fight; accuracy is what the measurement minigame reads; capability is the wall
